transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

On Samsung fridge-freezers, code 22E typically indicates an issue with the evaporator fan in the fridge section—either it isn't spinning because it's jammed by ice, or the motor has failed. This aligns with your symptom of the fridge side not being cold: if that fan can't push chilled air from the freezer into the fridge, the fridge warms up while the error flashes. This is often fixable without replacing parts immediately, as it's frequently caused by a defrost system fault (like a failed heater or thermostat) allowing ice to build up and block the fan. However, we need to confirm if the cooling system itself is still working before deciding on repairs. Could you please check:
1. Is the freezer compartment still cold enough for frozen food?
2. Inside the freezer, is there a thick block of frost or ice on the back wall (behind the panel)? Once I know that, I can guide you through the next safe checks.
Freezer side is fine, still frozen solid. I haven't looked at the back wall of the freezer though - the only frost I've seen is a bit around the vent at the top back of the fridge side.

The fact that your freezer is still frozen solid while the fridge is warm suggests the cooling system itself (the compressor) is working, but the cold air isn't reaching the fridge compartment. On Samsung models like yours, code 22E usually points to the evaporator fan in the fridge section not spinning correctly. This most commonly happens because a defrost fault has allowed ice to build up on the coils inside the freezer back panel. The ice blocks the airflow into the fridge and can also jam the fan blades or prevent it from being detected by the sensor, triggering the 22E code. The small amount of frost you see at the top vent is consistent with this: air is trying to pass through but hitting a blockage. The most reliable way to confirm this—and potentially restore cooling temporarily—is to perform a full manual defrost. This will melt any ice blocking the fan or vents. Please switch the appliance off at the wall socket, remove all food (keeping it cold in cool bags), and leave both doors open for 24 hours until every bit of ice has melted. Dry everything thoroughly, then plug it back in. Once you have done this, let me know if the fridge side starts getting cold again within a few hours. If it does but the error returns or the fridge warms up again after a day or two, we will know for certain that a defrost component (like the heater or thermostat) has failed and needs replacing.

Ok, I did the full defrost with the doors open and used my cool box for the food. The code cleared and the fridge got cold again, but 22E came back about 10 days later. No burning smell or tripping at any point. What does that mean for the repair?

The fact that the fridge cooled perfectly after your manual defrost but the error returned within 10 days suggests this is not a random glitch or a simple blockage—it is a recurring fault in the automatic defrost system. Here is what is happening: Your freezer has an automatic cycle to melt ice from the cooling coils. One of the parts controlling this (usually the heater, the thermostat that triggers it, or the sensor that monitors temperature) has failed. Because the cycle isn't working properly, ice builds up on the coils inside the freezer back panel. This ice eventually blocks the airflow into your fridge section and can jam the fan, triggering the 22E code. Since we know the cooling system itself is fine (the freezer stays frozen), this is a repairable fault involving specific electrical components. To proceed safely and accurately, I need to see inside the freezer back panel where these parts are located. Please switch the appliance off at the wall socket again for safety. Remove the rear panel inside the freezer compartment. Look at the coils behind it. Are they covered in a thick block of ice, or do they look clear? Also, locate the white plastic heater element and any small metal disc with wires attached near it, and tell me exactly what you see. Note: If you are not comfortable removing panels or dealing with electrical components, please call an engineer. They will need to replace the failed defrost part(s) to stop this from happening again.

I can't remove the inner back panel and I'm not going to attempt it. I also don't have a multimeter. Is there anything else I can check, or should I get an engineer in? I bought it from Currys 3 years ago and have the receipt, but I don't know if any extended cover applies.

You should get an engineer in. Because you cannot remove the inner back panel to inspect the coils and components, there is no safe owner-level way to confirm exactly which part has failed or to carry out the repair. The pattern of symptoms—error 22E returning after a temporary fix from a manual defrost—is definitive for a fault in the automatic defrost system. This usually involves one of three internal parts: the defrost heater, the defrost thermostat (thermal fuse), or the temperature sensor. These are located behind the rear panel inside the freezer and require dismantling to access and replace. Regarding your purchase from Currys 3 years ago: standard manufacturer warranties on major appliances typically last for one year. Since it has been three years, you will likely need to pay for the engineer's call-out and parts unless you purchased a specific extended warranty or care plan at the time of sale (which would be detailed in your paperwork). If you have that cover, contact Currys customer service with your receipt; otherwise, you can book an independent appliance repair engineer directly.
